name: trend-full-reversion-half-current-config
rationale: Lead #2 of the 2026-10-22 report: across four variants on two runs, raising the trend weight improved the 500k diagnostics monotonically (trend 0.25 -> 0.5 -> 1.0 at reversion 1.0: -14.96% -> -7.26% -> -2.80%). This walks the curve past equal weights by halving the reversion family instead (trend 1.0 / reversion 0.5), on experiments/baseline-config.json exactly. Literature-motivated: Tang et al. (2024) measure the short-interval Hurst exponent of BTC rising from ~0.42 (2019-20) to ~0.49 (2021-22), i.e. the short-horizon anti-persistence that the reversion-heavy weighting was built on has largely disappeared; our own 1-minute lag-1 autocorrelation (-0.0146) is half the magnitude that motivated reversion dominance.
code_change_summary: In TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs), set TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT to 1.0 and REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT to 0.5. Nothing else changes: every sub-signal formula (RSI, damped SMA cross, damped EMA cross, damped MACD histogram / step fallback, Bollinger %B), the weighted-mean aggregation, the empty-sub_signals warmup guard, the non-positive SMA/EMA guards and the sentiment combination stay byte-for-byte identical. Update both constants' doc comments (and the compute_btc_target doc comment listing the weights) to record that this is a trend-dominant probe past equal weights, motivated by Tang et al. (2024, arXiv:2402.11930) and the monotonic trend-weight curve in the 2026-10-19/22 reports. Then update the expected values in the compute_btc_target_* unit tests wherever the new weights legitimately change them; any test asserting reversion dominance (e.g. compute_btc_target_mean_reverting_family_dominates_trend_disagreement) must be rewritten to assert the new arithmetic rather than deleted.
constraints: This hypothesis modifies the body of TradingEngine::compute_btc_target. This change MUST be made only on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch -- never as a direct commit to dev/main.
MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) -- only its body.
MUST NOT change any individual sub-signal's own formula or the aggregation expression; exactly the two weight constants change (TREND 0.25 -> 1.0, REVERSION 1.0 -> 0.5).

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the compute_btc_target_* unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs -- update their expected values if the new weight legitimately changes them (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body, so the reviewer gives it the scrutiny an allocation-formula change deserves.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or anything on the live order-submission path.

paper_reference.title: Stylized Facts of High-Frequency Bitcoin Time Series
paper_reference.authors: Yaoyue Tang, Karina Arias-Calluari, M. N. Najafi, Michael S. Harré, Fernando Alonso-Marroquin
paper_reference.key_claim: Intraday BTC returns are subdiffusive at short intervals, but the short-interval Hurst exponent rose from ~0.42 (2019-20) to ~0.49 (2021-22), indicating the short-horizon mean reversion has nearly vanished as the market became more efficient.
paper_reference.pros: Same asset, high-frequency intraday data, and a recent sample; directly bears on whether a reversion-dominant 1-minute weighting still has a basis, which our own trend-weight results question.
paper_reference.cons: Descriptive stylized-facts study with no trading strategy, fees or out-of-sample test; spot USD data rather than bitFlyer BTC/JPY; H ~0.49 implies near-random-walk, which argues against trend persistence too, not only against reversion.
